summary.document_title: PCI-DSS v4.0 Mandatory Security & Audit Specification
summary.executive_summary: Defines two mandatory Q4 PCI-DSS v4.0 audit requirements: AES-256-GCM envelope encryption for Redis session payloads (which directly conflicts with FIN-106) and an immutable HMAC-signed security audit log in AWS S3 Object Lock.
risks_and_dependencies: Existing backlog item FIN-106 proposes plaintext Redis caching, which would cause an immediate PCI-DSS v4.0 audit failure if merged.
AWS KMS key rotation policies and S3 Object Lock bucket provisioning require Security Operations approval.
open_questions: Does Legal & Compliance require a 7-year or 10-year cold archival retention window for S3 Object Lock audit logs?

stories.title: AES-256-GCM Envelope Encryption for Redis Checkout Session Payloads
stories.user_story: As a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), I want all cached checkout and cardholder session payloads in Redis encrypted with AES-256-GCM using AWS KMS per-tenant keys, so that the platform passes Q4 PCI-DSS v4.0 compliance.
stories.technical_description: Implement client-side AES-256-GCM envelope encryption with KMS data-key caching before writing any checkout payload to Redis, and block/supersede plaintext caching story FIN-106.
acceptance_criteria: Given any checkout session payload written to Redis, when inspected at rest, then all sensitive fields are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and include a KMS key version header.
Given a compromised or cross-tenant key context, when decryption is attempted, then GCM authentication tag verification fails and raises a SecurityViolationError.
Envelope encryption/decryption adds less than 3ms p99 latency overhead using local KMS data-key caching.
stories.priority_rationale: Mandatory Q4 PCI-DSS v4.0 audit blocker that prevents plaintext exposure of sensitive checkout data.
stories.alignment_notes: Directly conflicts with existing backlog item FIN-106 ('Plaintext Session Payload Caching in Shared Redis Cluster'). FIN-106 must be canceled or replaced by this encrypted implementation.

stories.title: Immutable HMAC-Signed Security Audit Trail in S3 Object Lock
stories.user_story: As a Compliance Auditor, I want every administrative privilege escalation, API key rotation, and SSO configuration change logged as an HMAC-SHA256 signed event in S3 Object Lock, so that audit trails are tamper-evident and verifiable.
stories.technical_description: Build an asynchronous audit sink that signs admin security events with HMAC-SHA256 and writes batched JSONL segments to an AWS S3 bucket configured in Compliance Object Lock mode.
acceptance_criteria: Given any RBAC privilege change, API key rotation, or SSO config update, when the action completes, then a signed JSON audit record is persisted within 5 seconds.
Given a stored audit batch in S3, when the verification CLI checks the HMAC-SHA256 chain, then any tampered or deleted record is immediately detected.
S3 bucket policy enforces Object Lock WORM protection preventing root/admin deletion prior to retention expiry.
stories.priority_rationale: Required for Q4 PCI-DSS v4.0 audit readiness and forensic traceability.
stories.alignment_notes: Net-new compliance audit logging requirement not currently represented in the backlog.
